title: introductory-microbiology Mindmap
notes: Kingdom Monera comprises prokaryotic organisms: bacteria, cyanobacteria, mycoplasma, and archaebacteria. Bacteria show diverse shapes, nutrition, and…
Kingdom Monera: prokaryotic organisms (no membrane-bound nucleus); includes bacteria, cyanobacteria (blue-green algae), mycoplasma, and archaebacteria.
Bacterial cell: capsule (slime layer) → cell wall (peptidoglycan) → plasma membrane → cytoplasm; 70S ribosomes; naked circular DNA (nucleoid); may have pili,…

subtopics.name: Key points
points: Monera = prokaryotic: no true nucleus, 70S ribosomes, circular DNA.
Shapes: cocci, bacilli, spirilla; arrangements: diplo-, strepto-, staphylo-.
Nutrition: autotrophic (photo/chemo) + heterotrophic (saprophytes, parasites).
Growth curve: lag, log, stationary, death.
Binary fission = asexual reproduction; conjugation/transformation/transduction = genetic exchange.

subtopics.name: Formulas & relations
points: Binary fission: 1 cell → 2 identical daughter cells (asexual)
Growth curve: N(t) = N₀ × 2ⁿ (n = number of generations in log phase)
Lag → Log → Stationary → Death
Gram +ve: thick peptidoglycan → retains crystal violet (purple); Gram -ve: thin + LPS → pink (safranin)

subtopics.name: Statements to quote
points: Bacteria are the oldest and most abundant life forms on Earth.
Binary fission is the primary mode of asexual reproduction in bacteria.
Cyanobacteria are photosynthetic prokaryotes that fix atmospheric nitrogen.

subtopics.name: Exam focus
points: Draw and label a typical bacterium — very common.
Describe the bacterial growth curve (4 phases).
Explain Gram-staining and differentiate +ve and -ve.
Monera = M-O-N (Micro, Osmotic, No nucleus).
Shapes: Cocci = round; Bacilli = rod; Spirilla = spiral.

subtopics.name: Common misconceptions
points: Bacteria are prokaryotic: they have no true nucleus and no membrane-bound organelles.
Cyanobacteria are bacteria (prokaryotes), NOT algae; they fix nitrogen but are not "true" algae.
Mycoplasma lacks a cell wall; it is the smallest known living cell.

subtopics.name: Key points
points: Bacterial cell: capsule → wall (peptidoglycan) → membrane → cytoplasm (nucleoid, plasmids, 70S ribosomes).
Gram +ve: thick peptidoglycan (purple); Gram -ve: thin + LPS (pink).
Shapes: cocci, bacilli, spirilla, spirochaetes; arrangements: diplo-, strepto-, staphylo-.
Nutrition: autotrophs (photo/chemo) + heterotrophs (saprophytes, parasites).
Growth curve: lag, log, stationary, death; generation time (E. coli ~20 min).

subtopics.name: Formulas & relations
points: Gram -ve: capsule + LPS + thin peptidoglycan + membrane + cytoplasm (70S ribosomes, plasmids, nucleoid)
Gram +ve: capsule + thick peptidoglycan + membrane + mesosomes + cytoplasm
Growth: lag → log (2ⁿ) → stationary → death
Genetic exchange: conjugation (F+ → F-), transformation (DNA uptake), transduction (phage)

subtopics.name: Statements to quote
points: The bacterial cell has a capsule, peptidoglycan wall, plasma membrane, and cytoplasm with a naked nucleoid.
Gram-positive bacteria have a thick peptidoglycan; Gram-negative have a thin one plus an outer LPS membrane.
Bacteria reproduce by binary fission and exchange genes by conjugation, transformation, and transduction.

subtopics.name: Exam focus
points: Draw and label a detailed Gram-negative bacterium.
Draw and label a Gram-positive bacterium.
Differentiate Gram +ve and -ve bacteria (4 points).
Bacterial cell = C-W-M-C (Capsule, Wall, Membrane, Cytoplasm).
Growth = lag, log, stationary, death (4 phases).

subtopics.name: Common misconceptions
points: Gram-positive = THICK peptidoglycan (retains crystal violet, purple); Gram-negative = THIN peptidoglycan +…
Mesosomes are invaginations of the plasma membrane; they are NOT true organelles (no membrane-bound…
Plasmids are small circular DNA; they are NOT the chromosome (nucleoid).

subtopics.name: Key points
points: rDNA: 7 steps (isolate, cut, ligate, transform, select, express, harvest).
Vectors: plasmids, phages, cosmids, BACs, YACs; features: ori, selectable marker, MCS.
Host cells: E. coli (prokaryotic), yeast (eukaryotic), mammalian cells.
Medical: insulin (1982), vaccines (HBV, HPV), monoclonal antibodies, gene therapy.
Agricultural: Bt crops, herbicide-tolerant crops, tissue culture, biofertilisers.

subtopics.name: Formulas & relations
points: rDNA: isolate → cut (restriction enzyme) → ligate (DNA ligase) → transform → select → express → harvest
Plasmid: ori + selectable marker + MCS + high copy number
Insulin: human gene → E. coli → fermentation → purification → insulin
CRISPR: guide RNA + Cas9 → cut DNA → repair → desired change

subtopics.name: Statements to quote
points: Recombinant DNA technology is the cornerstone of modern biotechnology.
The rDNA process follows 7 detailed steps.
Human insulin produced by E. coli was the first biotech drug (1982).

subtopics.name: Exam focus
points: Describe the 7 steps of rDNA technology in detail.
Explain the structure of a plasmid vector.
Explain the production of human insulin using rDNA.
Plasmid = ori + marker + MCS + copy number.
Insulin = E. coli = bacteria make human protein.

subtopics.name: Common misconceptions
points: Restriction enzymes CUT DNA at specific sequences; DNA ligase JOINS DNA fragments; they are different tools.
A plasmid is a small circular DNA molecule used as a VECTOR; it is NOT the gene of interest itself.
